explanation: Williams Syndrome is a deletion syndrome that occurs when a small end piece of Chromosome 7 is deleted. Children with this syndrome have a characteristic 'pixie-like' appearance, marked by turned-up noses, wide mouths, a small chin, and large ears. Academically, they often have poor skills, but they typically excel in verbal and musical abilities. The deletion causes the elastin gene to be missing, which leads to cardiovascular health problems and premature aging of the skin.

questions.q: Which chromosomal deletion causes Williams Syndrome, and what is the typical physical appearance of affected children?
opts: Deletion on chromosome 20; flat face and round head.
Deletion of a small end piece of Chromosome 7; 'pixie-like' appearance with turned-up nose, wide mouth, small chin, and large ears.
Deletion on the X chromosome; broad chest and webbed neck.
Deletion on chromosome 22; very tall stature and persistent acne.
